newsitem.title: USA: Ill. school faces yearend deadline to issue COPs.
newsitem.headline: Ill. school faces yearend deadline to issue COPs.

text.p: A U.S. District Court judge has stepped up the pressure on an Illinois school district by ordering it to issue nearly $50 million of certificates of participation by December 31.
Matthew Corby, associate superintendent of mangement services for the Rockford School District, said a court order was issued Friday requiring that the debt be sold.

He said the school district was working with Banc One Capital Corp to get the deal ready for market. However, he pointed out that a financial plan for dealing with the district's reoccuring operating deficits will not be ready until Dec. 20.
That plan has also been ordered by the courts. The district has an approximately $15 million deficit in its $200 million fiscal 1997 budget.

Corby said that the district might not have enough time to get the financial plan done and obtain the necessary insurance for the COPs to be issued by yearend. He added he did not know what would happen if the district fails to comply with the court order for selling the debt.

Another complication is the need to pass a $4.6 million annual property tax levy to pay off the COPs, Corby said. The school board is scheduled to take up the levy request at its meeting Tuesday night, he added.
If passed, the district's aggregate property tax levy would increase by 16.5 percent, according to Corby.

A federal judge last month initially ordered the COPs sale as a result of an ongoing desegregation case originally filed against the district in 1989. Proceeds from the COPs will be used to finance the construction of three new buildings.
The Rockford school district is currently unable to issue general obligation bonds to satisfy the order because of pending taxpayer lawsuit challenges to previous tax levies for liability issues.
